body.statement: For independent sample splits of sizes \(n_1,n_2\), \[\inf_{G_0,\Sigma_0}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\ge1-\alpha_1,\qquad \inf_{G_0,\Sigma_0}\Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\in\{\operatorname{SCC}(G):G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\}\ge1-\alpha_1.\] For every true \((\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in\Theta_{G_0}\) and every \(u,v\in V\) with \(u\ne v\), \(\Pr\{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\}\ge1-\alpha_2\) and \(\Pr\{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}\ge1-\alpha\).
body.justification: The set-valued construction keeps structural and parameter uncertainty visible instead of conditioning on one learned graph.
body.gap: Wang, Kolar, and Drton and Strieder et al. give DAG uncertainty procedures; SCC recovery alone does not identify coefficients, so this result unions over graphs and parameter roots.
body.consumer: A signaling analyst can report a feedback-module confidence set and a conservative equilibrium-intervention effect set without treating the selected graph as known.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We first establish a covariance bound that applies to either split.  Let \(q\in\mathbb N\), let \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and let \(S_q=q^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^qX_rX_r^\top\) for iid \(X_r\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_0)\).  For \(a,b,c,d\in V\), differentiation of the Gaussian moment-generating function
\[
 M(t)=\mathbb E\exp(t^\top X_1)=\exp\!\left(\frac12t^\top\Sigma_0t\right)
\]
four times at \(t=0\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[X_{1a}X_{1b}X_{1c}X_{1d}]
 =\Sigma_{0,ab}\Sigma_{0,cd}
  +\Sigma_{0,ac}\Sigma_{0,bd}
  +\Sigma_{0,ad}\Sigma_{0,bc}.
\]
Taking \(c=a\) and \(d=b\), and using \(\mathbb E[X_{1a}X_{1b}]=\Sigma_{0,ab}\), yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(X_{1a}X_{1b})
 =\Sigma_{0,aa}\Sigma_{0,bb}+\Sigma_{0,ab}^{\,2}.
\]
Independence across observations and entrywise unbiasedness of \(S_q\) therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
 &=\frac1q\sum_{a,b\in V}
   \left(\Sigma_{0,aa}\Sigma_{0,bb}+\Sigma_{0,ab}^{\,2}\right)\\
 &=\frac{(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_0)^2+\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^2)}q.
\end{aligned}
\]
The covariance eigenvalue-margin assumption gives \(\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_0)\le\overline M\).  Since \(\Sigma_0\) is positive definite and has \(p\) eigenvalues,
\[
 \operatorname{tr}\Sigma_0\le p\overline M,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^2)\le p\overline M^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Sigma_0}\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F^2
 \le \frac{p(p+1)\overline M^2}{q}.
\]
For every nonnegative random variable \(W\) and \(a>0\), the pointwise inequality \(W\ge a\mathbf 1\{W>a\}\) gives \(\Pr\{W>a\}\le\mathbb E[W]/a\) after taking expectations.  Apply this inequality with \(W=\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F^2\) and \(a=r_q(\gamma)^2\).  The definition of the Gaussian covariance radius then gives
\[
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\!\left\{\|S_q-\Sigma_0\|_F>r_q(\gamma)\right\}
 \le
 \frac{p(p+1)\overline M^2/q}{r_q(\gamma)^2}
 =\gamma.
 \tag{1}
\]
This bound is uniform over every \(G_0\in\mathcal F\) and \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\), because its right-hand side uses only the common eigenvalue margin.

Apply \((1)\) to the first split with \((q,\gamma)=(n_1,\alpha_1)\), and write
\[
 \mathcal E_1
 :=\left\{\|S_{n_1}-\Sigma_0\|_F\le r_{n_1}(\alpha_1)\right\}.
\]
The iid Gaussian sampling assumption and \((1)\) imply \(\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_1)\ge1-\alpha_1\).  Because \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\), the definition of distance to a set gives, on \(\mathcal E_1\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_F(S_{n_1},\mathcal M_{G_0})
 =\inf_{A\in\mathcal M_{G_0}}\|S_{n_1}-A\|_F
 \le\|S_{n_1}-\Sigma_0\|_F
 \le r_{n_1}(\alpha_1).
\]
By the definition of the split-sample structural set, \(\mathcal E_1\subseteq\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\ge1-\alpha_1.
 \tag{2}
\]
Whenever \(G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\), its partition \(\operatorname{SCC}(G_0)\) is one member of \(\{\operatorname{SCC}(G):G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\}\).  Thus the event in \((2)\) is contained in the corresponding SCC-coverage event.  Taking the infimum of these two bounds over \(G_0\in\mathcal F\) and \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M_{G_0}\) proves both displayed first-split inequalities.

We next verify that the effect construction is well defined.  Fix \(G\in\mathcal F\), \((\Lambda_G,\omega)\in\Theta_G\), and distinct \(u,v\in V\).  If \(J_u:\mathbb R^{V\setminus\{u\}}\to\mathbb R^V\) is the coordinate isometry, then \(\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}=J_u^\top\Lambda_GJ_u\).  The stability-margin assumption therefore gives
\[
 \|\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le\|\Lambda_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le1-\kappa<1.
\]
For \(B=\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top\), the finite geometric identity gives
\[
 (I-B)\sum_{k=0}^N B^k=I-B^{N+1},
 \qquad
 \|B^{N+1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le(1-\kappa)^{N+1}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Passing to the operator-norm limit proves that
\[
 (I-\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top)^{-1}
 =\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\Lambda_{G,-u,-u}^\top)^k.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the equilibrium perfect-intervention derivative in its definition is finite and is continuous in \(\Lambda_G\).  The same stability bound makes \(I_p-\Lambda_G\) invertible, so the covariance map is continuous on \(\Theta_G\).  By the compact-parameter assumption, each set \(C_G\), being the intersection of \(\Theta_G\) with the inverse image of a closed Frobenius ball under this continuous covariance map, is compact.  Hence, whenever \(C_G\ne\varnothing\), continuity following from \((3)\) makes the infimum and supremum in the definition of \(\mathcal I_{u\to v}\) finite and attained.  These extrema, and therefore the coverage event below, are measurable: for a fixed real \(c\), the set of covariance matrices \(S\) for which there exists \((\Lambda,\omega')\in\Theta_G\) satisfying both \(\|S-\Sigma_G(\Lambda,\omega')\|_F\le r_{n_2}(\alpha_2)\) and \(\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda)\le c\) is closed, because any convergent sequence of such \(S\)'s has a corresponding convergent subsequence of witnesses in compact \(\Theta_G\); the analogous assertion holds with \(\tau_{u\to v}^G(\Lambda)\ge c\).  A finite union over \(G\in\mathcal F\) is Borel measurable.

Now fix a true \(\theta_0=(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in\Theta_{G_0}\).  By the covariance-map and model-image definitions, being true for the sampling law means
\[
 \Sigma_0=\Sigma_{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)
 =\omega(I_p-\Lambda_{G_0})^{-\top}(I_p-\Lambda_{G_0})^{-1}
 \in\mathcal M_{G_0}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Apply \((1)\) to the independent second split with \((q,\gamma)=(n_2,\alpha_2)\), and define
\[
 \mathcal E_2
 :=\left\{\|S_{n_2}-\Sigma_0\|_F\le r_{n_2}(\alpha_2)\right\}.
\]
Then \(\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_2)\ge1-\alpha_2\).  Equation \((4)\) and the definition of \(C_{G_0}\) show that
\[
 \mathcal E_2
 \subseteq
 \{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\},
\]
and consequently
\[
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{(\Lambda_{G_0},\omega)\in C_{G_0}\}
 \ge1-\alpha_2.
 \tag{5}
\]

On \(\mathcal E_1\cap\mathcal E_2\), the graph \(G_0\) belongs to \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha_1}\), the set \(C_{G_0}\) is nonempty, and \(\theta_0\in C_{G_0}\).  Therefore
\[
 \inf_{(\Lambda,\omega')\in C_{G_0}}
 \tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda)
 \le
 \tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})
 \le
 \sup_{(\Lambda,\omega')\in C_{G_0}}
 \tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda).
\]
The interval on the left and right is one of the sets in the union defining \(\mathcal I_{u\to v}\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal E_1\cap\mathcal E_2
 \subseteq
 \{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}.
\]
Finally, \(\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_1^c\cup\mathcal E_2^c}\le\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_1^c}+\mathbf 1_{\mathcal E_2^c}\); taking expectations and using the split-level assumption gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{\Sigma_0}\{\tau_{u\to v}^{G_0}(\Lambda_{G_0})\in\mathcal I_{u\to v}\}
 &\ge \Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_1\cap\mathcal E_2)\\
 &\ge1-\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_1^c)-\Pr_{\Sigma_0}(\mathcal E_2^c)\\
 &\ge1-\alpha_1-\alpha_2\\
 &\ge1-\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This last argument does not require more than the two marginal bounds, although the asserted independent splitting supplies the stated iid Gaussian law on each split.  Together with \((2)\) and \((5)\), this proves every claim.
